rules.label: Private residential garage use
rules.explanation: For a principal residential use, the code permits a private garage for storage of not more than four motor vehicles. This is a use rule, not a complete site-feasibility approval.
unresolved: Base zoning and site-specific overlays can add development standards.
Vehicle-storage use does not determine dimensional compliance or permit requirements.

rules.label: Base site-development standards for SF-1, SF-2 and SF-3
rules.explanation: Austin's current site-development table lists the base front, street-side, interior-side and rear setbacks plus building and impervious-cover limits for each zoning district. More specific rules can supersede a base value.
unresolved: A more specific use/district rule, overlay or site condition may supersede a base standard.
The current property building/impervious percentages require clipped spatial calculations before comparison.
Garages and carports count toward building and impervious cover under current City guidance.

rules.label: Detached accessory structure building-permit exemption
rules.explanation: Austin lists a residential building-permit exemption for a one-story detached accessory structure only when it is no more than 200 square feet, no more than 15 feet high, creates no dwelling, contains no plumbing, and is not in a flood hazard area. The structure must still comply with applicable codes and ordinances.
unresolved: Electrical, plumbing, floodplain or other approvals may still apply depending on project scope.
Failing the exemption conditions means this exemption does not apply; the full permit path must still be confirmed.

rules.label: Rear setback for low accessory buildings in SF-1, SF-2 and SF-3
rules.explanation: For SF-1, SF-2 and SF-3 districts, the Land Development Code states a five-foot rear-yard setback for an accessory building that is not more than one story or 15 feet in height.
unresolved: Easements, overlays, special area regulations and other site conditions can require additional review.
A taller or multi-story structure must be evaluated under the otherwise applicable regulations.

rules.label: Garage placement relative to the front lot line and building façade
rules.explanation: Austin's garage-placement rule says a parking structure may not be closer to the front lot line than the front-most exterior wall of the first-floor building façade. A second width condition applies when a garage entrance faces a front yard abutting public right-of-way and the parking structure is less than 20 feet behind the building façade. The City posted an updated interpretation in 2026.
unresolved: The beta does not yet derive the front lot line, front-most first-floor façade or garage entrance orientation from authoritative geometry.
Neighborhood-plan or other combining-district conditions may require additional applicability review.
